reference.title: Certificate Alias Credential
reference.shortdesc: When configuring secure communication for Fox, Web, or Platform services, you select a Certificate Alias from the User Key Store. This alias identifies which certificate is used for authentication and encryption.

section.p:
When setting the certificate alias, you have two options for the private key password:
Unique password: This allows you to specify a unique password for the private key associated with this certificate alias. Use this if you require different passwords for different certificates or want to override the global setting.
Use global certificate password: This option uses a password that is globally configured for all certificates in the system. This simplifies management, but for higher security, unique passwords are recommended.The password is required to retrieve the private key from the User Key Store during authentication or when importing a signed certificate.

section.title: How client certificate authentication works

ul.li: Client certificate authentication uses the private key of a client certificate stored in the User Key Store of the station (the client).

When the client connects to a server, it presents its certificate. The server, which holds the corresponding public certificate, verifies that the client possesses the private key by challenging it to sign data or decrypt a message.
This process ensures that only clients with the correct private key can authenticate, providing strong mutual authentication.

section.p: For more details, see the "Certificates and credentials" chapter in the .
